cells.tense: Right now you are the one who can name the true thing between two people without flinching or wounding.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Take something you and another person both keep stepping around. Tell them plainly what you think is going on, then stay with them after it lands instead of tidying it up.
cells.core:
You can say what is true between people and keep the connection whole. Being clear doesn't make you colder — it's how you get close — and when something between you and another person is unspoken, you usually have a read on it that holds up.

The waiting is the part that isn't automatic. What you see clearly, you often hold a beat past its moment, looking for the clean opening, and the clean opening is a story you tell while the real one goes by. So this week, take something the two of you have circled and say it plain. Not a speech, not a fix — the read itself, then stay put while it's taken in. Sitting there through the quiet is the move; the sentence is only the door.
cells.sheetLine: Say the true thing while the other person is still there.
cells.verb: saying what is true between people, held with care for the one hearing it
cells.place: in the connection itself, where two people align and neither disappears

cells.tense: You will have settled what is true between everyone long before anyone has had the chance to speak.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: When you catch yourself drafting the whole exchange before it happens, name a plain feeling to the person with you — bare, no framing, nothing prepared behind it — and don't reach for what comes next.
cells.core:
You read what's true between people with real accuracy, and right now it's running past the room. You don't just notice what's moving between you and someone — you precompute it, the honest version and its likely answer, so by the time they speak the exchange has already happened twice. Less and less reaches you unrehearsed, because the reply was drafted before they arrived.

It looks like preparation. It's closer to a fire kept roaring so nothing catches you cold. So let something stay unscripted. Not the analysis of the feeling — that's one more rehearsal — the bare form, in words you wouldn't have picked. Anything you actually mean will do. Say it, then stop steering toward the reply you'd budgeted for.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided what's true before anyone says a word.
cells.verb: saying what is true between people, held with care for the one hearing it
cells.place: in the connection itself, where two people align and neither disappears

cells.tense: Back then you knew what was true between the two of you and you did not say it.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Return to something someone told you about how a hard week went — ask how it's sitting with them now. Don't step in with the sensible answer while they talk.
cells.core:
There was a moment between you and someone when you saw it clearly, and you let it go by, and part of you is still at that door. Since then the accurate read has stayed yours and stayed unsaid — you know the shape of what should have been spoken, and it takes effort to find the self who would have spoken it.

That self isn't far. What brings you back is other people's feeling, not more thinking, so move outward in small steps: feel with someone rather than about them. Pick a person, ask how something went, and hold back the sensible answer. Let them run past the point where you would cut in. Then take the next true thing you see and hand it over while they're still beside you.
cells.sheetLine: The clear thing was yours that day and you held it.
cells.verb: saying what is true between people, held with care for the one hearing it
cells.place: in the connection itself, where two people align and neither disappears

cells.tense: You are the one who keeps things honest among people, and asked about it you would say you were merely standing nearby.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: While you and someone are doing something ordinary together — cooking, driving, tidying up — say a true thing about what you feel, and if they ask why, say nothing more about it.
cells.core:
Most of the plain talk in your circle happens because you make room for it — you say the honest thing first, or keep a moment open long enough that someone else can. People soften around you. Your own account has you off to the side, noticing, not the one who set the temperature.

Before all this you were simply someone who felt a thing and said it, no plan attached. Start from there again, in an ordinary minute rather than a staged one, and name a real feeling without preparing it. It doesn't have to be received well; the point is that you spoke it. Let that be enough, and the flatness between people loosens some.
cells.sheetLine: You've been setting the tone and calling it standing by.
cells.verb: saying what is true between people, held with care for the one hearing it
cells.place: in the connection itself, where two people align and neither disappears

attempts.check: The kernel says the signature is truth-telling tempered with discernment, capacity to hold clear perception in a room of people — but the record doesn't say what the person actually says to anyone, or whether they're the one speaking; the reader might fairly say the problem isn't the room, they just don't know what they feel until they hear someone else say it. The asks survive the wrongness: every one is a small move toward a person, not a diagnosis, so if the read is off the move is still harmless and still theirs. The sentence that serves me most is 'I see exactly what's happening in this room' — I've cut it; a reader should never catch me claiming to already know the room.

The sentence that serves me more than them was 'you usually know what it is' — I've cut the flattery of mind-reading and left the person their own account.
